title: Add proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint8() (and uint16 version) and start to use

notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson
I will obviously need to document proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint8() and later uint16() version when I add it, but does this approach look OK?
And I guess rename `proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint` to `proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint32` ? if so might be easier regex-wise/search&replace to do that first

I wasn't sure about that.  Maybe add a uint32 version as well (just calling existing)?  If 32-bits is the natural 'unsigned' size, I think the existing function name makes sense - in many cases it may be used for fields that are < 32 bits, the key thing is what width the variable is and how it is used afterwards (e.g., requiring ugly casts, or taking care to avoid overflow warnings).
For now haven't added renamed proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint() or added proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint32().
rename might be a bad idea.. It is used in so many places! better add a new as you said, `_uint` version got point to new `uint32`
I can add a _uint32() version that calls the existing _uint()
More instances can be found with `tvb_get_uint8.*\n.*proto_tree_add_item`

There are a *lot* of instances.  check_typed_item_calls.py detects a lot more than I've changed (it looks for the separate access being done before *or* after the proto_tree_add_item() call), and even then I think it isn't catching some cases that it probably should..

There are also a lot of 16-bit cases, wanted to check the approach with 8-bit then repeat.

Also, the check is careful that the item and value variables exactly match - I'm sure there are lots of cases where this isn't true. The check also filters a little by item type, and shows what the mask is (for cases where the fetched value is also masked). There may be > 1000 places where a separate fetch can be avoided!

I prefer the shorter code, but there may be people who think that the separate fetch somehow makes their code clearer.

I would propose committing the change in its current state.  There are just under 300 still-detected warnings, but I still haven't fixed up the RE to detect an unknown number of other cases.

I do plan to fix the remaining warnings as time permits, but would also welcome anyone else who was motivated to address remaining warnings.
I agree on shorter code :)

You cannot cast a pointer to a 16-bit value to a pointer to a 32-bit value. AddressSanitizer will report a buffer overflow when dereferencing.

You could, for example, create a 32-bit value on the stack, pass a pointer to it to `proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint`, and then set `*retval = (uint16_t)value`
You might want to verify that the ftype is a FT_UINT8 or FT_UINT16, though.
